title: release-provenance --pre mishandles X-rc.N launcher versions: checks platforms at rc strings, rcs eat the --limit window
description:
Found by the LCLI-625 reviewer (2026-09-28); recorded by the LCLI-625 implementer from the reviewer's report. Out of LCLI-625's scope, which kept --pre unchanged.

MECHANISM (scripts/release-provenance.mjs runPre, read at LCLI-625 branch head): --pre lists versions from the LAUNCHER's packument and checks every package of releasePackages() at each version string. Since LCLI-621 the launcher stages as X-rc.N, so that packument gains X-rc.N versions. parseVersion strips the prerelease suffix, so an rc is not filtered as unparseable or below the baseline. Consequences: (1) each rc is checked against all seven packages, and the six platform rows name versions like @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64@X-rc.N that will never exist; they report 'absent', which is loud but not red. (2) Each rc consumes a slot in the --limit window (default 10), pushing earlier releases' platform packages out of it. (3) The platforms at X are not re-checked until promote-latest.mjs puts X in the launcher's packument, and never for an abandoned rc that is never promoted.

REVIEWER'S SCRATCH MEASUREMENT (relayed, not re-run by the filer): against a stub packument [0.7.0, 0.7.1, 0.8.0-rc.1, 0.8.0-rc.2, 0.8.0-rc.3] with --limit 3, --pre checks only the three rcs against every package, never reaches 0.7.1, and exits 0.

TIMING: latent today, because no -rc launcher is on the registry yet. It must land before the first publish:true Release run under LCLI-621, since that run's rc is the first to enter the packument.

acceptanceCriteria.text: --pre never queries a platform package at an X-rc.N version: a test with a stub packument containing X-rc.N launcher versions asserts from the stub request log that no platform@X-rc.N attestation is requested
--pre re-verifies the platform packages at X for a release whose launcher packument holds only X-rc.N (staged, not yet promoted, or abandoned), proven by a test
The --limit window counts releases, not rc strings: with the reviewer packument [0.7.0, 0.7.1, 0.8.0-rc.1..3] and --limit 3, --pre reaches 0.7.1, and a test pins it
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change

plan: Measure the relayed scratch claim against the pre-fix script (stub packument [0.7.0, 0.7.1, 0.8.0-rc.1..3], --limit 3) and record the request log
runPre: group launcher packument versions into releases by numeric core X; order releases by X and, within one, X-rc.N by numeric N, other suffixes by string, X last; never via compareVersions
Per release: platforms at X exactly once (even when only rcs are published), launcher at each version it actually has exactly once; --limit counts releases; baseline decided on X
Tests pinning AC1-AC3 from the stub request log, plus order/dedup; mutation-prove each AC; gates incl. win32 preload; CHANGELOG + runbook provenance-pre paragraph
implementationNotes: For the implementer (LCLI-625 delta reviewer, 2026-09-28): compareVersions treats X-rc.N and X as equal (parseVersion strips the suffix), so within --pre their order follows the packument key order. Harmless once this task counts releases rather than rc strings, but do not rely on the sort to separate them.

RELEASE GATE (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-28 ~04:33Z): required before the first publish:true Release run under LCLI-621. The first such run puts the first X-rc.N into @opum-ai/lore's packument, which is what activates this defect. Recorded as priority high and as a dependency of LCLI-621.

PRE-FIX MEASUREMENT (re-run here, not relayed; scripts/release-provenance.mjs at origin/dev 58dcb391, node v24.20.0, bun 1.3.14): a scratch Bun stub serving packument [0.7.0, 0.7.1, 0.8.0-rc.1, 0.8.0-rc.2, 0.8.0-rc.3] with every attestation 404, running 'node scripts/release-provenance.mjs --pre --limit 3' with the default package set. Exit 0. 21 attestation requests: @opum-ai/lore and all six platform packages at each of 0.8.0-rc.1, 0.8.0-rc.2, 0.8.0-rc.3, and nothing else. 18 of the 21 name a platform at an rc string. 0.7.0 and 0.7.1 are never requested, and no platform is requested at 0.8.0. The header read '5 to re-verify, taking the most recent 3 x 7 package(s)'. That confirms the reviewer's claim as relayed. Registry today (npm view, read-only): neither @opum-ai/lore nor @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64 lists any prerelease version, so the defect is still latent.

IMPLEMENTED on fix/LCLI-627-pre-rc-versions (not yet a PR; AC4's reviewer pass is outstanding). DESIGN: runPre groups the launcher packument by numeric core X (groupReleases). Per release it checks platforms at X only, once, even for an rc-only release, and the launcher at each version it has, once each (preReleaseSpecs). --limit slices release groups. Baseline is decided on X, so X-rc.N of a baseline release is baseline, which agrees with semver precedence against a release baseline. ORDER is set in groupReleases, never by compareVersions, which calls X-rc.N and X equal: releases by numeric X, unparseable after; within a release X-rc.N by numeric N, then other suffixes by string, then X last. A suffix other than -rc.N gets a ::warning:: and is checked launcher-only. Unparseable versions keep their old handling (own group, all packages at the string). Zero-in-scope still hits report()'s VERIFIED NOTHING path. POST-FIX, same scratch stub (reviewer packument, --limit 3): 23 requests, being the launcher and six platforms at 0.7.0 and 0.7.1, the launcher at 0.8.0-rc.1..3, and six platforms at 0.8.0. No platform was requested at an rc string, and the launcher was not requested at 0.8.0. CONTROL: the seven new tests against origin/dev's script went 7 red, with the 41 existing tests green. MUTATION (predicted first, each matched exactly): M1 AC1 revert (platforms also at each non-X launcher string) gave 5 red, {AC1, exact-set, order/dedup, odd-suffix, baseline-rcs}. M2 AC2 revert (platforms at X only when launcher X is published) gave 3 red, {exact-set, AC2, baseline-rcs}. M3 AC3 revert (window over strings, then regroup) gave 2 red, {AC3, order/dedup}. M4 (rc N compared as strings) gave 1 red, {order/dedup}. All 41 pre-existing tests stayed green in every mutant. GATES (lore 0.11.0 from source, quest 0.11.0, bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0): bun test exit 0 (4296 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail); bun run typecheck 0; bun run lint 0 (3 pre-existing warnings in other files); bun run lore check 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings); bun run lint:shell 0. release-provenance.test.ts under a bun --preload that sets process.platform to win32 exited 0 (48 pass). Caveat: the preload reaches the bun test process only, not the node child that runs the script.
